findings.body:
<!-- proofline:finding-series=01a202cc-13e9-71f9-9a26-d4fd26f725f8 -->
**Warning** · Concurrent upgrades can abort a console command before dispatch

Two invocations can both read version 1. After one commits migration 002, the other still runs `CREATE INDEX` and fails because the index already exists.

The second console command exits without running.

Acquire a write transaction before reading `user_version` and execute the migration within that same transaction.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The duplicate-index failure on version-1 databases is new. Before this change, the same stale-version check could race during initial schema creation, but version-1 databases skipped all migrations.

</details>

[View finding in Proofline](https://proofline.sh/orgs/by-id/01a202a0-cd61-7684-99bc-53c775b0de50/reviews/01a202ca-cdb7-707c-895f-6b59429bfd1d/findings/01a202cc-13eb-75d8-8975-7e127b2f51fa)

findings.body:
<!-- proofline:finding-series=01a202cc-13ea-72cd-a349-211abff056b7 -->
**Warning** · First history page after upgrade waits for a full table scan

On a version-1 database, `history` synchronously builds the pending index, scanning every `deliveries` row even when none are pending.

A default first page that previously visited at most 21 rows must now wait for one million extra row visits on a million-row database.

Build the index in an explicit upgrade step rather than on `history` startup.

[View finding in Proofline](https://proofline.sh/orgs/by-id/01a202a0-cd61-7684-99bc-53c775b0de50/reviews/01a202ca-cdb7-707c-895f-6b59429bfd1d/findings/01a202cc-13f4-7034-a75b-9452c6eca119)
